name: Theudas
overview: Theudas was a male figure known for leading a revolt, a movement that ultimately ended with his death. Scripture identifies him as someone who rose up against the established order, as noted in Acts 5:36. No tribal affiliation or additional personal details are recorded about him.
namesAndTitles: Theudas is the sole name recorded for this individual, with no specific meaning or divine origin provided in the biblical text. The name itself does not reveal further insight beyond identifying him as the leader of a failed uprising.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships for Theudas beyond his role as a leader who revolted. There are no known relatives or connections mentioned in the biblical account.
scriptureSignificance: Theudas is significant in the biblical narrative as an example of a failed revolutionary figure who attempted to challenge the established authorities but was ultimately killed. His story serves as a cautionary reference in the context of early Christian history, illustrating the dangers and consequences of such uprisings. His mention in Acts 5:36 highlights the contrast between earthly movements and the enduring kingdom of God.
